title: add JSONSchema response_format strict mode + improved validation errors and streaming compatibility
author: Aditi Rao
description: Adds JSONSchema-backed response_format support with a strict mode and improved validation/error handling. Motivation: customers are asking for deterministic, machine-readable outputs (structured output) and clearer diagnostics when models deviate from the schema. This change implements: 1) a new 'response_format' API option that accepts a JSON Schema reference (or inline schema) and a 'strict' boolean; 2) server-side validation for final and streaming output with configurable failure handling policies (reject, best-effort, sanitize); 3) improved error messages surfaced through the API (error.code, error.message, error.schema_path) and bridges the behavior with the OpenAI-compat layer so OSS clients see similar types for schema validation failures; 4) streaming compatibility: partial validation is performed for streamed chunks and a final validation pass is performed before marking a streaming response as complete; 5) test coverage and integration test harness updates for strict/non-strict scenarios; 6) developer docs and API spec updates. Checklist: - [x] RFC + design doc linked (ENG-5623) - [x] Implementation of response_format parsing and schema registry hooks - [x] Server-side validation and strict mode enforcement - [x] Streaming validation + fallback policies - [x] OpenAI-compat behavior parity tests - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs and examples updated Note: default behavior remains backward compatible (no schema validation unless response_format provided). When strict=true and validation fails, the request will return 400 with structured error payload. When strict=false, the platform will attempt best-effort corrections (e.g. coerce types, remove invalid fields) and include validation_warnings in the response metadata. For streaming, if partial chunks fail validation and strict=true the stream is truncated and an error frame is emitted. See release_notes for user-facing changes. Related PRs: pr-51234 (openai-compat schema layer), pr-48273 (initial strict response validation experiments).

review_comments: Samir Patel: Overall looks good. A few questions: can you decouple schema registry lookups from request handling to avoid added latency? Also please add metrics for schema validation latency and failure rate.
Aditi Rao: Addressed by adding async cache and pre-warm hooks in jsonschema_validator.py; added metrics 'schema.validation.latency' and 'schema.validation.failures' in the dashboard yaml.

Lena Thompson: Streaming behavior needs to be explicit in the API spec — what happens to partial tokens? Recommend an error frame with code SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED and a final 'validation_status' field in the meta payload.
Aditi Rao: Added stream error frame + final status field. Updated openai_compat mapping to include 'type': 'validation_error' to match client expectations.

Diego Morales: Tests look thorough. One nit: in non-strict mode we should document the sanitization heuristics (coerce primitives, drop unknown fields). Also ensure audit logs contain the original model output when sanitization happens.
Aditi Rao: Added sanitization doc section and audit log hook; updated integration tests to assert presence of original_output in audit logs when sanitization occurs.
release_notes: Add response_format JSON Schema support with strict mode and improved validation errors: - New 'response_format' API accepts JSON Schema + strict flag. - strict=true: validation failures return 400 with structured error (code: SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED). - strict=false: best-effort sanitization with validation_warnings included in metadata; original output retained in audit logs. - Streaming: partial validation for chunks; on strict failures stream emits error frame and truncates. - OpenAI-compat layer maps validation failures to compatible error objects. See docs for examples and migration notes.
notes: Perf: validation path is optimized (schema cache + precompiled validators). In perf-sensitive workloads enable pre-warm and local registry replication. No change to token billing.
